clue.text: Having wine on board is outrageous

indicators.note: the ship 'has' the wine aboard, so one piece is held inside the other

parts.note: being on board means being on a ship, and SS stands for steamship
hock is a German white wine

explanation.surface: A drinks cargo carried on deck causes a scandal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On board' is crossword shorthand for inside a ship; 'Having' signals the containment, and 'outrageous' looks like an adjective but goes with 'is' as a verb phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Something outrageous scandalises people, so 'is outrageous' is a verb phrase meaning causes outrage.

clue.text: Funny sort of fences!

definitions.meaning: laughs written out are funny noises
a ha-ha is a sunken fence or ditch in a landscaped park

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims at strange fencing.
explanation.definitionFit: Bursts of laughter, and sunken ditches that act as park boundaries without blocking the view.

clue.text: Despite its name it makes plagiarism an offence

definitions.text: Despite its name it makes plagiarism an offence

parts.words: Despite its name it makes plagiarism an offence
parts.note: the name seems to grant the right to copy, yet this legal protection forbids copying

explanation.surface: A law whose title belies its purpose bans literary theft.
explanation.definitionFit: The legal ownership of a creative work that makes copying it without permission unlawful.

clue.text: Silvia had their universal commendation

parts.note: the song in Two Gentlemen of Verona, Who is Silvia?, says all the young country lovers praise her

explanation.surface: A woman named Silvia was praised by everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: Shakespeare's song runs 'Who is Silvia? what is she, That all our swains commend her?'
explanation.definitionFit: Rustic youths and lovers, as in pastoral poetry, who in the song all commend Silvia.

clue.text: What a monstrous water-spout!

parts.note: read as an exclamation at a big jet of water, but it describes a grotesque carved creature on a church roof that spouts rainwater

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims at a huge jet of water.
explanation.definitionFit: Carved stone monsters on cathedrals serve as rainwater spouts, throwing water clear of the walls.

clue.text: Midas's parting gift ?

parts.note: King Midas turned all he touched to gold, so his farewell clasp would be gilded; also a generous payoff to a departing executive

explanation.surface: A rich king's farewell present.
explanation.definitionFit: A large severance payment to a departing executive, imagined as a literal golden clasp of hands.

clue.text: Bad fish causing pain

parts.note: rank food is bad, gone off
the ling is a cod-like sea fish

explanation.surface: Spoiled seafood makes someone ill.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that rankles causes lasting resentment and soreness.

clue.text: Times description, far from modern in 5 dn

indicators.note: the answer is found within the letters of the other entry, so the surrounding letters are dropped

parts.note: refers to the entry at 5 down, a phrase for a big payoff

explanation.surface: The newspaper describes something as old-fashioned in a cross-reference.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop the opening G and the second word HANDSHAKE from the answer at 5 down. 'Times' looks like the newspaper but belongs to a phrase about days of yore.
explanation.definitionFit: Ancient days are called the olden times, so the word means bygone.

clue.text: Is he irritable in company?

parts.note: liverish means irritable, and a member of a City of London guild is a man of a livery company

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a man is grumpy around others.
explanation.walkthrough: City of London guilds are called livery companies; 'livery' once also meant bad-tempered, as from a disordered liver.
explanation.definitionFit: A freeman of one of the City of London guilds, which wear distinctive livery.

clue.text: Downcast as one cast down

parts.note: a chap is a person, one fellow
something cast down has fallen

explanation.surface: Someone is dejected, like a person thrown to the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Dispirited and dejected, literally with the jaw hanging slack.

clue.text: Rich man, short of a shilling, may plunge

indicators.note: being short of something means lacking it, so a letter is dropped

parts.note: Dives is the rich man in the Bible parable of the beggar Lazarus
s was the abbreviation for the old British shilling coin

explanation.surface: A wealthy man who runs low on cash may take a dive.
explanation.walkthrough: The shilling was a pre-decimal British coin, abbreviated s.
explanation.definitionFit: To plunge headlong into water is to make a dive.

clue.text: Reg's neat trick may repel

indicators.note: a trick plays games with the letters, rearranging them

parts.note: the name with its s kept as a letter
taken as written

explanation.surface: A clever stunt by someone called Reg might put people off.
explanation.definitionFit: To alienate or drive someone away is to push them off emotionally.

clue.text: Kipling's ladies in transports

definitions.meaning: Kipling wrote a poem calling the ocean steamship a lady
passenger ships carry travellers across oceans

explanation.surface: The women of Kipling's stories are in raptures.
explanation.definitionFit: Ocean-going passenger ships are vessels of transport, and Kipling's verse 'The Liner She's a Lady' calls such a ship a lady.

clue.text: Piper's bird ?

definitions.meaning: a piper here is a pipe smoker, and his stuff is coarse cut tobacco

explanation.surface: A bagpiper owns a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: Coarse tobacco cut in strands is what fills a pipe, and the crested cormorant is a seabird of the same name.

clue.text: It sounds an infernally tedious bloomer (could be a stinker)

indicators.note: the clue says the plant name is heard like other words

parts.note: hell for infernally and bore for tedious, run together

explanation.surface: Something seems a hellishly dull mistake, possibly a dreadful one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloomer' looks like a blunder but means a flowering plant; one species is called the stinking hellebore.
explanation.definitionFit: A winter-flowering plant, one species of which is called stinking for its smell.

clue.text: Workers love me, being so liberal

parts.note: farm or factory hands are workers
love is zero in tennis, shaped like the letter O
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone claims the staff adore them for their generosity.
explanation.definitionFit: A generous amount is a handsome one, so liberal giving fits.

clue.text: Put up with the two quarters permitted

parts.note: south is a quarter of the compass
west is another compass quarter
permitted means allowed

explanation.surface: Someone tolerated the pair of districts being allowed.
explanation.definitionFit: To accept or tolerate something unwelcome, as when you swallow an insult.

clue.text: Gave press prominence to pass held with difficulty

indicators.note: the letters struggle into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Newspapers made a big story of a hard-won pass.
explanation.definitionFit: A newspaper that splashes a story runs it in big headlines.

clue.text: Certain keys used by a fixer in a tizzy

parts.note: musical keys with flats in their signatures, such as B flat
a pin fixes things together

explanation.surface: A locksmith fumbles with some keys while flustered.
explanation.definitionFit: An aircraft spinning out of control, figuratively a state of panic and agitation.

clue.text: Florence's flower produced on artist's return

indicators.note: a return goes back the way it came, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: A Florentine bloom is shown when the painter comes back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower' is a river, something that flows; 'return' turns ON and RA as one run. RA stands for a Royal Academician.
explanation.definitionFit: The river running through Florence, a flower in the sense of something that flows.

clue.text: Once it wasn't cricket for a gentleman to be an actor

definitions.text: Once it wasn't cricket for a gentleman to be
definitions.meaning: in English cricket gentlemen were amateurs and the paid professionals were the other side, so a gentleman could not be one

explanation.surface: It was once improper for a gentleman to go on the stage.
explanation.walkthrough: English cricket had a Gentlemen v Players match until 1962, pitting amateurs against professionals.
explanation.definitionFit: A professional cricketer, as opposed to the amateur gentleman, and also a stage performer.

clue.text: I ran into one

parts.note: read as bumping into someone, but the two opening words run together into a country name, which is what an older name for that land became

explanation.surface: Someone admits a collision with a person.
explanation.definitionFit: The old name for the country renamed in 1935 as I-RAN, the two words of the clue joined.

clue.text: Sounds bright and cheerful, the Prophet's follower

indicators.note: the clue says the answer is heard like another word

parts.note: a sunny disposition is bright and cheerful

explanation.surface: A follower of Muhammad seems happy.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of the larger branch of Islam, followers of the Prophet's custom.

clue.text: Malvolio's sickness fatal to Narcissus

definitions.meaning: in Twelfth Night Olivia tells Malvolio he is sick of vanity
Narcissus pined away adoring his reflection

explanation.surface: A Shakespearean steward's illness proved deadly to a Greek youth.
explanation.definitionFit: Vanity and narcissism, the excessive admiration of oneself.

clue.text: Scientist from upper part of Africa ?

definitions.meaning: Alessandro ..., the Italian physicist who invented the electric battery
Upper ... was a West African country, now Burkina Faso

explanation.surface: A researcher comes from northern Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: Upper Volta is the former name of Burkina Faso; the clue lets 'upper' look like 'northern'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian physicist who gave his name to the volt, and the river naming the colony of Upper Volta.

clue.text: It's the fate of Scandinavia to lack a navy

parts.note: no means lacking any, as in no money
RN is the Royal Navy

explanation.surface: Doomed Nordic nations have no fleet.
explanation.definitionFit: In Norse mythology the three goddesses of destiny are called by this name.

clue.text: Pompous dandy unpopular with cruise passengers?

definitions.meaning: heavy means pompous and a swell is a dandy
big rolling waves at sea make passengers seasick

explanation.surface: An overbearing fop is disliked by those aboard ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A pompous dandy is heavy plus swell, and a heavy swell is rough rolling sea that cruise travellers dread.

clue.text: Use ignition once more

parts.note: a plain instruction to light a fire again

explanation.surface: An instruction to start the engine again.
explanation.definitionFit: To set alight again, as a dying fire or a lost passion.

clue.text: Bad communist press infuriates one sort of speculator

definitions.meaning: red means communist and a rag is a poor newspaper
a bull is a speculator who buys expecting rises, and a bull is said to be maddened by a scarlet cloth

explanation.surface: A shoddy left-wing newspaper enrages a stock market trader.
explanation.definitionFit: A poor communist paper is a red rag, and a red rag to a bull is proverbially provoking.
